name: CustomFields.com – Custom Fields & Custom Post Types
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
CustomFields.com is a WordPress custom fields plugin for structured content. Build field groups, create custom post types and taxonomies, and give editors clear places to enter the details your website needs. Display saved content with Gutenberg blocks, shortcodes or PHP templates.

Free includes all 26 field types, including repeater fields, flexible content, galleries, relationships and reusable groups. Custom post types, custom taxonomies and options pages are included too. No account or licence is required for Free.

Try the Free and Pro live demos

Explore the actual plugin in a temporary WordPress site with fictional sample content:

  • Try the Free demo — Build and edit fields, save content in the WordPress editor, and view the frontend result.
  • Try the Pro demo — Explore the listing builder, submission review, bulk editing and CSV workflows alongside Free.

No signup or payment is needed. Pro access is included for the temporary demo; licence activation and payments are unavailable there. Changes expire with the session. Use sample information, not personal or confidential data. Demo privacy and limits.

Build field groups with repeaters and conditional logic

  • Create field groups visually with starter kits, drag-and-drop ordering and input previews.
  • Add text, rich text, numbers, dates, images, files, galleries and choice fields.
  • Use repeater fields for rows of content and flexible content for rows with different layouts.
  • Show fields conditionally and validate entries. Hidden fields retain their saved values.
  • Place fields on posts, pages, custom post types, user profiles and existing taxonomy terms.

Organize content with custom post types and taxonomies

Create a custom post type (CPT) for projects or team members. Organize records with custom taxonomies and connect them using relationship fields. Keep shared site information on named options pages. Configure these structures in the admin interface.

For example, use a portrait and job title for team profiles, dates and galleries for a project portfolio, repeater rows for specifications, or an options page for shared contact details. These are content structures you can build; your theme or chosen display method controls their presentation.

Display custom fields in Gutenberg, shortcodes or templates

Use the Custom field block in the WordPress block editor (Gutenberg) for saved text and media. The Custom field repeater block displays selected direct children as a list or table. Free also lets you create named blocks with their own controls and values.

The Use your fields guide provides a field picker and Copy shortcode action. Add format="html" to render images, file links and galleries; existing plain shortcodes keep their original output. PHP helpers, block bindings and authenticated REST integration are included for developers. Nested collections and more complex layouts need an appropriate template.

Compare CSV data, check content and migrate supported fields

Free includes read-only CSV comparisons, content checks, JSON definition imports, schema history and compatible field revisions. Review supported migrations from ACF, Secure Custom Fields or Meta Box while preserving source values. Templates and arbitrary third-party structures are not automatically converted. Check the adapter limits and test a migration on staging first.

What the separate Pro add-on adds

Pro adds the directory/listing builder, visitor search, reviewed CSV updates, submission forms with approval, bulk editing, deployment, content transfers and scheduled checks with report history. Existing saved listings render in Free; creating or changing listing definitions requires activated Pro. Free CSV comparison reviews data without applying updates.

On your own site, Pro requires Free and one successful licence activation. Optional marketing choices are separate. The hosted Pro demo provides temporary access; it does not include a licence for your own installation.

Getting started | Display your fields | All documentation | Compare Free and Pro | Free support

Related plugins from Plugins.shop

Optional tools from our team, installed separately. They are not required by CustomFields.com and do not automatically connect to its fields.

  • CatalogFAQ – FAQ accordions and reusable answers — Reuse answers across content pages. WooCommerce is required only for product FAQ features.
  • KillerConversions – WordPress contact form builder — Collect enquiries and project briefs in local WordPress entries.
  • Logged.ai – WordPress activity log — Review supported content and settings changes when investigating site edits.

Privacy

To time an optional review reminder, the plugin stores the first successful field-save time, up to three distinct UTC usage dates, and the reminder choice for each administrator on this site. It does not store field values in that record, track page visits or send this information off site. Remind me in 30 days postpones the request; Don’t ask again or opening the review form stops future reminders. Opening that form does not tell the plugin whether a review was submitted. Review reminder settings lets you change your choice. The record persists across updates and is included in WordPress personal-data export and erasure for the matching account. Opening WordPress.org is a deliberate visit to an external website.

Free content tools need no account or external service. Goals, display preferences, private CSV comparisons, content checks and optional workflow counts remain on your WordPress site. Optional counts are off by default. A deliberately selected Pro workflow is remembered locally for seven days; preview visits are not tracked. Optional welcome choices are described separately below. WordPress personal-data tools include current registered profile values for the matching WordPress account and matching email tokens in saved Free CSV checks. CSV erasure clears derived comparisons; unrelated source cells remain. Retained or damaged data is reported for administrator review. Removed definitions, other content, historical storage, backups and separate Pro workflow history may require manual review; see README.md for scope.

Source code and development

The complete, readable PHP, JavaScript and CSS source is included in this plugin. The files under assets/ (including nested directories) are the editable source and are loaded directly by WordPress; there are no separate minified bundles or missing build inputs. No compilation, npm or Composer installation is required. See the bundled SOURCE.txt for source locations, editing and packaging steps, optional syntax checks, translation commands and dependency attribution.

Self-hosted DM Sans fonts are licensed under SIL OFL 1.1; see assets/fonts/OFL.txt. Font project source: https://github.com/googlefonts/dm-fonts

Optional welcome service

After a meaningful save, CustomFields offers two independent, initially unchecked choices. You can continue without sharing and use every Free tool. Reopen Welcome choices from the plugin workspace at any time.

Domain registration sends only the displayed public hostname to https://customfields.com/newsletter-api/v1/customfields-welcome/ with a random connection identifier, authentication token, consent version and request timestamp. It does not send the full URL, WordPress/PHP versions, language, edition, field definitions or content. The registration expires after 90 days unless you explicitly refresh it. No background registration or status requests run. The server sees ordinary network connection information such as the source IP.

Email signup independently sends your entered email address and the same kind of consent/connection metadata to that service. Email-only signup does not attach the site domain in its payload or User-Agent. Inbox confirmation is required before new marketing email eligibility. An existing subscriber keeps their preferences; a submitted request does not guarantee a new confirmation email.

Use the separate Remove site registration and Stop these emails actions to withdraw a linked choice. Email withdrawal stops this connection’s own confirmed signup; independently existing subscriptions remain managed through their email preference/unsubscribe links. Failed withdrawals retain a local retry option and do not silently resubmit enrollment. Deactivating or removing the plugin is not a remote unsubscribe request.

Local saved choices, the selected domain/email and protected request credentials remain in this WordPress database until you remove that choice. A matching WordPress personal-data erasure request can also remove the email choice; domain registration is independent. Remote expiry does not automatically erase the local record. A removal attempt immediately clears its local domain/email payload; a protected request credential and, for email retry matching, a keyed email reference can remain until remote removal is confirmed.

Domain records are retained for up to 90 days. Pending newsletter requests expire after 48 hours; confirmed subscriptions follow the newsletter retention policy. Withdrawal markers prevent delayed requests from reinstating withdrawn choices. These choices are independent of Pro licence activation and optional update checks.

Privacy: https://customfields.com/privacy/
Newsletter choices and retention: https://customfields.com/newsletter/privacy
Terms: https://customfields.com/terms/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate CustomFields.com – Custom Fields & Custom Post Types.
  2. Create a field group, choose where it appears and save.
  3. Choose Enter values, complete the fields in the matching WordPress editor and save the content.
  4. Preview saved values, then follow the group-specific block, shortcode or template instructions to display them.

Back up before updating. Update Free to 1.2.6 first. If you use Pro, keep it installed and check your account for an eligible add-on update after updating Free. Do not uninstall to upgrade. For the earlier customfields folder, deactivate that Free copy before activating customfields-com and keep it inactive. Saved data retains its identifiers.
sections.faq:
Can I try Free and Pro before installing?

Yes. Open the Free or Pro live demo linked above to use the actual plugin in a temporary WordPress site. No signup or payment is needed. Use the fictional sample content, save your changes and check the frontend output. The session expiry and demo limits are shown before you start; work is not kept permanently. The installed Free plugin is not time-limited.

Do I need to write code?

You can build field groups, register content types and enter values through the admin interface. Use the included field and repeater blocks or supported shortcodes for basic output. Complex layouts, nested collections and relationship lists need an appropriate template; this plugin does not replace your theme or provide an unrestricted page builder.

Are repeater fields and custom post types free?

Yes. All 26 field types, repeaters, flexible content, relationships, custom post types, taxonomies and options pages are included in Free. No account or licence is required. Pro adds the separate workflows listed above.

How do I display a custom field on a page?

Save a value, then insert the Custom field block or copy its shortcode from Use your fields. For example, [customfield name="job_title"] displays a saved scalar value. The field group must match the current content. Developers can also use the bundled PHP helpers.

Why does an image shortcode show an attachment ID?

Plain shortcodes preserve their original text or ID output. Use [customfield name="portrait" format="html"] for an image field; the same format supports file links and galleries. Uppercase HTML and surrounding spaces are accepted. Other format values, including “url”, are unsupported and retain the original output. Media output respects attachment access.

How do I display repeater rows?

Insert the Custom field repeater block, choose a matching repeater and select the direct child fields to display as a list or table. You can choose fields before saving a new post or page, but the preview uses saved values. Nested groups and flexible layouts need templates; a plain repeater shortcode does not render a collection.

Why do some fields show a code or an ID?

Single-choice fields keep their stored key, and related-post, user and term fields keep their stored ID. The html format adds media markup and rich-text output; it does not turn every reference into a title or link. Use a template for relationship lists and nested collections. Existing shortcode output is preserved when you update.

Does it work with Elementor?

Elementor Free supports the field-value and saved-listing widgets. Creating or changing a listing requires CustomFields.com Pro. The dynamic tag requires Elementor’s own supported edition, normally Elementor Pro; no Elementor licence is included.

Can I import existing fields and values?

JSON definition imports and supported value migrations are separate, reviewed workflows. Source values are preserved. Existing theme templates and arbitrary third-party structures are not automatically converted. Check the bundled developer guide for adapter limits and test on staging. SCF 6.9.8 can deny source metadata access by default; see docs/SCF-CONVERSION.md for the explicit authorization requirement.

What happens when I deactivate the plugin or Pro expires?

Stored definitions and content are retained; plugin-powered tools require the relevant plugin to run. Activated local Pro tools continue through ordinary expiry or temporary outages. Explicit disconnection locks new Pro work and pauses workers. Active entitlement governs private downloads and support.

What limits should I check before a larger project?

Schemas allow 100 groups, 200 fields per group, three composite levels and 1 MB JSON imports. Hosting limits can be smaller. Comment, menu and network-settings targets are not supported. See README.md and docs/FEATURE-REFERENCE.md for permissions, storage, rendering and migration limits.
sections.changelog:
1.2.6

  • Improve editor validation feedback, preview focus, relationship controls and options-page navigation. Confirm removal actions, keep rich-text markup valid, and polish responsive controls and catalogue wording. Existing field values and shortcode output are retained.

1.2.5

  • Add a neutral WordPress.org review link in Help & updates for administrators.
  • Offer a small review reminder after 30 days and successful field saves on three distinct days, with snooze and permanent dismissal.
  • Keep review preferences local to each account and site, with personal-data export and erasure support.

1.2.4

  • Restore relationship settings for newly added and saved fields in the main builder.
  • Explain migration source-access failures and preserve source and destination permission checks.
  • Show completed and restored migration states without idle automatic-run controls.
  • Warn early about unsupported options storage and clarify relationship, display and Free/Pro documentation.

1.2.3

  • Recheck attachment access when rendering media and authored blocks.
  • Isolate broken linked definitions so unrelated field groups remain writable.
  • Add personal-data handling for registered user fields and saved Free CSV checks; contain malformed welcome choices.

1.2.2

  • Accept uppercase and whitespace around the formatted shortcode option, preserving legacy output.
  • Keep image, file and gallery shortcodes valid inside paragraphs.
  • Make deliberate field opening easier to leave and clarify saved-value previews.

1.2.1

  • Display images, files and galleries with an opt-in formatted shortcode. Existing shortcodes keep their output.
  • Add the Free Custom field repeater block with chosen child fields and list or table layouts.
  • Open matching fields deliberately from the WordPress editor and use field-specific display guidance.

1.2.0

  • Add native Plugins.shop attribution and a bundled More Plugins collection.
  • Add a per-account Pro previews switch in Free; installed Pro keeps its own tools and licence navigation.
  • Align numeric conditional comparison text between PHP and the browser without rewriting saved rules or values.
  • Require explicit confirmation in the field builder before changing a saved storage key. Existing values are retained, not moved.
  • Add a field picker and Copy shortcode action to Use your fields, and link onboarding goals to explicit starter-kit choices.

Earlier release notes are included in changelog.txt.
